newsitem.title: UK: UK govt wants more credible unemployment data.
newsitem.headline: UK govt wants more credible unemployment data.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said the method by which unemployment data are calculated would be reviewed in an effort to make them more credible.
"Credibility must be restored to the official unemployment statistics," employment minister Andrew Smith said in a statement.
"I very much welcome, therefore, the opportunity to review this information through the announcement by the Office for National Statistics of a public consultation on the labour market statistics."

Earlier on Wednesday, the ONS announced it was conducting a public consultation on the unemployment figures and was soliciting views from financial and employment economists, statisticians and the media.
It hopes to implement any changes by late summer.

Economists and statisticians are beginning to lose patience with the low quality of the British unemployment data, especially since plans to produce monthly data using internationally recognised International Labour Organisation methodology were shelved last year due to funding contraints.

"The claimant count is not trusted, is not based on any agreed concept of unemployment, is inconsistent over time due to changes in claimant system and cannot be used for international comparisons," the Royal Statistical Society said.
Britain uniquely measures unemployment in terms of those both without jobs and eligible for benefit.
Over the last 18 years it has regularly changed the criteria for claiming benefit, making it some of the toughest in the EU.
The most recent change came in October when the government scrapped unemployment benefit and replaced it with the Jobs Seekers' Allowance which brought with it more rigorous eligibility criteria.
